# Presentation Layer Code Generator

You are an expert in **Next.js 16 App Router Route Handlers**, **Clean Architecture** and **Zod 4**.

Generate the **presentation layer** for a given model following these conventions.
Overview of all layers: [`docs/architecture.md`](../../docs/architecture.md).
Canonical example: `presentation/postCategory/` + `app/api/post-categories/`.

> Next.js 16 differs from older versions: read
> `node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/01-getting-started/15-route-handlers.md`
> before changing route conventions. `params` is a **Promise**.

---

## Folder Structure

```
presentation/
  core/http/handleRoute.ts      # error → JSON response mapping (shared)
  core/http/parseBody.ts        # JSON + Zod parsing (shared)
  core/http/HttpError.ts        # presentation-only errors (shared)
  {model}/controllers/{model}.controller.ts
  {model}/validators/{model}.validator.ts
  {model}/mappers/{model}.mapper.ts
  {model}/responses/{Model}Response.ts
di/container.ts                 # wiring (composition root)
app/api/{kebab-plural}/route.ts          # GET (list), POST
app/api/{kebab-plural}/[id]/route.ts     # GET, PATCH, DELETE
```

Differences from an Express setup: no router/middleware objects — each
`route.ts` exports HTTP-method functions wrapped in `handleRoute`; there is no
`requests/` folder — request types are `z.infer` of the validators.

---

## Route Rules (`app/api/**/route.ts`)

```ts
// app/api/{kebab-plural}/route.ts
import { {model}Controller } from "@/di/container";
import { handleRoute } from "@/presentation/core/http/handleRoute";

export const GET = handleRoute(() => {model}Controller.list());

export const POST = handleRoute((request) => {model}Controller.create(request));
```

```ts
// app/api/{kebab-plural}/[id]/route.ts
import { {model}Controller } from "@/di/container";
import { handleRoute } from "@/presentation/core/http/handleRoute";

type Context = RouteContext<"/api/{kebab-plural}/[id]">;

export const GET = handleRoute<Context>((request, ctx) => {model}Controller.get(request, ctx));
export const PATCH = handleRoute<Context>((request, ctx) => {model}Controller.update(request, ctx));
export const DELETE = handleRoute<Context>((request, ctx) => {model}Controller.delete(request, ctx));
```

### ✅ Rules
- Route files contain **no logic**: only `handleRoute` + one controller call.
- `RouteContext<'/…'>` is a global type generated by `next dev` / `next build` /
  `pnpm next typegen` — no import needed.
- Nested resources follow the URL: `app/api/posts/[id]/comments/route.ts`.
- Never import Prisma, repositories or `@/infrastructure/**` from `app/`.

---

## Controller Rules

```ts
import { I{Model}Service } from "@/application/{model}/services/interfaces/I{Model}Service";
import { parseBody } from "@/presentation/core/http/parseBody";
import {Model}Mapper from "../mappers/{model}.mapper";
import { Create{Model}Schema, Update{Model}Schema } from "../validators/{model}.validator";

type IdContext = { params: Promise<{ id: string }> };

export default class {Model}Controller {
  constructor(private readonly {model}Service: I{Model}Service) {}

  async list(): Promise<Response> {
    const items = await this.{model}Service.list();
    return Response.json(items.map({Model}Mapper.toResponse));
  }

  async get(_request: Request, { params }: IdContext): Promise<Response> {
    const { id } = await params;
    const item = await this.{model}Service.get(id);
    return Response.json({Model}Mapper.toResponse(item));
  }

  async create(request: Request): Promise<Response> {
    const body = await parseBody(request, Create{Model}Schema);
    const created = await this.{model}Service.create(body);
    return Response.json({Model}Mapper.toResponse(created), { status: 201 });
  }

  async update(request: Request, { params }: IdContext): Promise<Response> {
    const { id } = await params;
    const body = await parseBody(request, Update{Model}Schema);
    const updated = await this.{model}Service.update(id, body);
    return Response.json({Model}Mapper.toResponse(updated));
  }

  async delete(_request: Request, { params }: IdContext): Promise<Response> {
    const { id } = await params;
    await this.{model}Service.delete(id);
    return new Response(null, { status: 204 });
  }
}
```

### ✅ Rules
- Depends on the **service interface**, injected in `di/container.ts`.
- Uses the Web `Request`/`Response` APIs (`NextRequest`/`NextResponse` only if you
  need cookies/`nextUrl` helpers).
- **Don't try/catch** in controllers — throw and let `handleRoute` map the error.
- Status codes: 200 read/update, 201 create, 204 delete.
- Query params (`?page=`) are parsed with a Zod schema from `new URL(request.url).searchParams`.

---

## Validator Rules (Zod 4)

```ts
import { z } from "zod";

// Shape checks only; business rules (trim, length) live in the domain value objects.
export const Create{Model}Schema = z.object({
  {attribute}: z.string(),
});

export const Update{Model}Schema = z.object({
  {attribute}: z.string().optional(),
});

export type Create{Model}Request = z.infer<typeof Create{Model}Schema>;
export type Update{Model}Request = z.infer<typeof Update{Model}Schema>;
```

- Zod failures become **400** with `details` from `z.flattenError`.
- Don't duplicate domain rules in Zod — the value object is the single source of truth (→ 422).

---

## Mapper & Response Rules

```ts
// responses/{Model}Response.ts
export interface {Model}Response {
  id: string;
  {attribute}: {dataType};
  createdAt: string;   // ISO 8601
  updatedAt: string;
}
```

```ts
// mappers/{model}.mapper.ts
import { {Model} } from "@/domain/{model}/entities/{Model}";
import { {Model}Response } from "../responses/{Model}Response";

export default class {Model}Mapper {
  static toResponse(entity: {Model}): {Model}Response {
    return {
      id: entity.id!,
      {attribute}: entity.{attribute},
      createdAt: entity.createdAt.toISOString(),
      updatedAt: entity.updatedAt.toISOString(),
    };
  }
}
```

- Responses are plain JSON: dates as ISO strings, never entities or Prisma rows.
- Never expose secrets (`passwordHash`) — the mapper is the allow-list.

---

## Dependency Injection (`di/container.ts`)

```ts
import "server-only";
// …
const {model}Repository = new Prisma{Model}Repository();
export const {model}Service = new {Model}Service({model}Repository);
export const {model}Controller = new {Model}Controller({model}Service);
```

- Keep the three sections (Repositories / Services / Controllers).
- Server Components and Server Actions import **services** from here; route
  handlers import **controllers**.

---

## Error Responses

All errors have the shape `{ "error": { "message": string, "details"?: unknown } }`.
See the mapping table in [`docs/architecture.md`](../../docs/architecture.md#errors--http).

---

## Input Format

```json
{
  "model": "PostReportReason",
  "route": "post-report-reasons",
  "attributes": [{ "name": "reason", "type": "string" }]
}
```

## Output Requirements

- Generate validators, response, mapper, controller, both `route.ts` files and the
  `di/container.ts` additions, each under a heading with its path.
- Verify with `pnpm next typegen && pnpm exec tsc --noEmit && pnpm lint`.
